bodyEn: Mikel Arteta’s reaction said it all. As Max Dowman trudged towards the touchline after becoming the youngest player sent off in a League Cup match at 16 years and 300 days, the Arsenal manager could not help himself.

Arms folded across his chest like an angry father who has caught his teenage son sneaking in after midnight, Arteta leaned over and aimed a few choice words in Dowman’s direction before the forward headed sheepishly down the tunnel. What he said remains unknown, although that hasn’t stopped the amateur lip-readers speculating on social media. “Get in the changing room. Now,” appears the most likely guess.

There is no doubt Arteta had made up his mind about the incident that ended with Dowman seeing red for reacting to an overaggressive sliding tackle from Fleetwood’s Harrison Neal. Although Arsenal intend to appeal and Arteta told Sky after the shock penalty shootout defeat by the League Two side 84 places below them in the pyramid that he wanted to watch it again before “assessing the situation”, the Spaniard made no excuses for Dowman in his post-match press conference.

“It was something that we discussed before the game,” he said when asked about their touchline exchange. “We knew when we prepared the context of the match, we were very clear on the things to expect, the things that emotionally we have to dominate.”

Whether Dowman’s reaction warranted a straight red card remains open to debate given there was minimal force when he lifted his right knee towards Neal. The referee, Michael Salisbury, could easily have decided to give both players a yellow and defused the situation, especially given Cole Palmer was booked for barging into Tottenham’s Matheus Fernandes off the ball on Saturday in what seemed a far more aggressive act. But, as Wayne Rooney and David Beckham infamously found to their cost while playing for England at the World Cup, acts of petulance are not usually tolerated by officials. Dowman was deemed to have overstepped the line.

It is a pressure Arteta has warned the record-breaking teenager would have to deal with as Dowman’s reputation has grown. Only last month Dowman was sent off playing for England Under-19s against the USA after a poorly timed tackle that most present at the behind-closed-doors match deemed a harsh decision. He was said to have been on the receiving end of a host of strong challenges in that match. Last year, Arteta urged Dowman to follow the example of Bukayo Saka after revealing Dowman was fouled nine times in a the first half of an England Under‑19s game against Spain.

“It’s going to happen, he’s going to have to learn when to release the ball and when to attract his starting position,” Arteta said. “Very similar to Bukayo in the beginning as well. Those players are going to attract players, contact, attention and they have to be very smart about when you want that contact and when you don’t want it, and what you have to do to avoid it.”

Asked how Dowman tends to react, he said: “He just gets up … very rare! Sometimes I get surprised emotionally how cool he can be. I think it’s about repetition. He’s so used to it that now he knows to let the referee deal with it and my teammates probably to defend me, and I will carry on playing.”

When the dust settles after a seismic defeat that ranks alongside Arsenal’s League Cup upsets against Swindon, Birmingham and Bradford, Arteta may come to regret such a public admonishment of a 16-year-old. His actions were criticised by Paul Merson, who questioned whether Areta would “do it differently” given another chance. But part of Arteta’s frustration will be that Dowman took the bait. He also knows opponents will now target Dowman even more to see whether they can provoke a reaction.

If Arsenal’s appeal fails, Dowman’s immediate punishment will be a three-match domestic suspension, causing him to miss Sunday’s trip to Liverpool and games against Hull and Newcastle. The timing is far from helpful: Saka’s thigh injury, expected to keep him out for several weeks, had opened up the possibility of more game time in the Premier League and Noni Madueke did not travel to Fleetwood owing to an ankle issue.

Dowman burst on to the scene last year by becoming the first 15-year-old to play in the Champions League, then broke the Premier League’s youngest goalscorer record against Everton in March, and this is the first major setback in his fledgling career.

He has been training with the first team since he was 14 and Arsenal have been extremely careful not to overexpose one of the most talked about players to emerge from their Hale End academy. Arteta resisted the temptation to give him many more minutes in the Premier League after Dowman scored twice against Ipswich in the previous round of the Carabao Cup last month. The challenge will be how Dowman responds to the extra scrutiny – on and off the pitch – that is bound to come his way.

items.titleZh: 马克斯·道曼与弗リート伍德的冲突让阿森纳与阿尔特塔感到尴尬
items.summaryZh: 道曼在联赛杯中染红引发关注，阿尔特塔赛后对此进行了严厉批评。
bodyZh: 米克尔·阿尔特塔的反应说明了一切。当16岁零300天的马克斯·道曼成为联赛杯中被罚下的最年轻球员，步履蹒跚地走向场边时，这位阿森纳主帅按捺不住自己的情绪。
阿尔特塔双臂交叉在胸前，就像一个抓到十几岁的儿子半夜偷偷溜回家的愤怒父亲，他俯身朝道曼的方向说了几句狠话，随后这位前锋灰溜溜地走进了球员通道。他说的话目前不得而知，但这并没有阻止业余唇语专家在社交媒体上进行猜测。“回更衣室去。现在，”这似乎是最有可能的猜测。
毫无疑问，阿尔特塔已经对这起事件做出了决定。此前，弗リート伍德球员哈里森·尼尔（Harrison Neal）的动作过大，道曼因做出反应而吃到红牌。尽管阿森纳打算上诉，且这家比阿森纳低84个名次的英乙球队在点球大战中爆冷淘汰阿森纳后，阿尔特塔在接受天空体育采访时表示他想先看回放再“评估形势”，但在赛后新闻发布会上，这位西班牙主帅并没有为道曼找借口。
当被问及他们场边的交流时，他说：“这是我们在赛前讨论过的事情。当我们准备这场比赛的背景时，我们对应该预料到的事情以及我们在情感上必须控制的事情非常清楚。”
考虑到道曼将右膝抬向尼尔时力量微乎其微，他的反应是否理应直接吃到红牌仍有待商榷。主裁判迈克尔·萨利斯伯里本可以轻易决定向两名球员出示黄牌以平息事态，尤其是考虑到科尔·帕尔默周六在无球状态下撞击热刺球员马特乌斯·费尔南德斯时只吃到黄牌，这看起来是一个更具侵略性的动作。但是，正如韦恩·鲁尼和大卫·贝克汉姆当年代表英格兰队参加世界杯时付出沉重代价一样，官员们通常不会容忍任性的行为。道曼被认为越界了。
阿尔特塔曾警告过这位打破纪录的少年，随着道曼名声的增长，他将不得不应对这种压力。就在上个月，道曼代表英格兰U19对阵美国队时，因一次时机不佳的铲球而被罚下场，当时在场的多数人都认为这是一次严厉的判罚。据说他在那场比赛中多次遭到凶狠的拼抢。去年，阿尔特塔敦促道曼以布卡约·萨卡为榜样，此前他透露道曼在英格兰U19对阵西班牙的上半场比赛中被侵犯了九次。
阿尔特塔说：“这种事还会发生，他必须学会什么时候出球，什么时候吸引防守位置。这和布卡约刚出道时非常相似。这些球员会吸引防守球员、身体接触和注意力，他们必须非常聪明，知道什么时候需要这种接触，什么时候不需要，以及该怎么做才能避免。”
当被问及道曼通常如何反应时，他说：“他只是站起来……非常罕见！有时他在情绪上能表现得如此冷静，这让我感到惊讶。我认为这是重复的力量。他已经习以为常，现在他知道让裁判去处理，队友大概会保护我，然后我会继续踢球。”
在一场与阿森纳此前在联赛杯对阵斯温顿、伯明翰和布拉德福德的爆冷失利相提并论的震撼失利尘埃落定之后，阿尔特塔可能会对公开斥责一名16岁球员感到后悔。他的行为受到了保罗·默森的批评，后者质疑阿尔特塔如果再有一次机会是否会“做得不同”。但阿尔特塔感到沮丧的部分原因在于道曼上了钩。他也知道，对手现在会更加针对道曼，看看能否激怒他。

推广后内容
如果阿森纳的上诉失败，道曼受到的即时惩罚将是国内禁赛三场，这将导致他错过周日对阵利物浦的比赛，以及对阵赫尔城和纽卡斯尔的比赛。这个时机非常糟糕：萨卡的腿筋受伤预计将让他缺阵数周，这本为他在英超联赛中获得更多出场时间创造了可能，而农尼·马杜埃凯由于脚踝问题并未随队前往弗リート伍德。
道曼去年崭露头角，成为在欧冠出场的最年轻15岁球员，随后在3月份对阵埃弗顿的比赛中打破了英超最年轻进球纪录，这是他刚起步的职业生涯中遭遇的第一个重大挫折。
他从14岁起就一直在随一线队训练，阿森纳一直非常小心，避免过度使用这位从黑尔端青训营走出来的备受瞩目的球员。在上个月联赛杯上一轮对阵伊普斯维奇打进两球后，阿尔特塔克制住了在英超联赛中给他更多出场时间的诱惑。接下来的挑战将是，道曼将如何应对随之而来的场内外的额外审视。

If you fail to scan your away match ticket, Arsenal will not receive information that you attended the fixture, and the away match loyalty point that has been credited to your membership account will be removed for the relevant away game.

items.titleEn: Coaching for Life
items.summaryEn: The Arsenal Foundation works with Save the Children on our Coaching for Life programme at the Za’atari refugee camp in Jordan
bodyEn: The Arsenal Foundation has worked in partnership with Save the Children since 2011, building pitches in some of the world’s toughest places so that young people who have faced violence, persecution and hardship can have safe spaces in which to play and learn.

In 2019 we combined our expertise to launch Coaching for Life, our programme at the Za’atari refugee camp in Jordan, home to displaced Syrians who have fled the civil war. Since March 2011, millions of young people have been displaced by Syria’s brutal civil war and many have witnessed horrors no child should ever see.

Coaching for Life combines more than 100 years of Save the Children’s child protection expertise and 40 years of Arsenal in the Community’s sports for development experience to build vulnerable young people’s mental, emotional and physical wellbeing through football.

In doing so, we are delivering a community programme to one of the toughest environments in the world. The goal was and remains clear: together we give children back their childhoods, provide them with the tools to rebuild their lives and coach them towards a better future. And since Coaching for Life started, more than 5,780 children have graduated from the programme.

Our work in Islington informs our approach in Jordan. Coaches in Za’atari include students from our Coach Development Programme, a two-year course based at The Arsenal Hub that offers comprehensive education from our team of experienced coaches and industry experts and involves leading and supporting sessions across our range of Arsenal in the Community projects at home and abroad.

Arsenal coaches work with Save the Children’s protection team and local coaches on how to use football to support children’s physical, mental and emotional wellbeing. This is much more than football coaching, however. The project gives children a voice and encourages them to stand up for their right to be safe and protected.

As Arsenal Academy manager and Foundation ambassador Per Mertesacker said after visiting the programme in Jordan, “When children suffer, we all lose. This project will give them courage to cope with the struggles they face day to day, as well as providing them with the skills to have a better future. Children are our future and we need to stand side by side with them.”
The impact of coaching for life has been profound. Since its launch some of the key statistics include…
•48 Syrian coaches trained – including 36 former participants – in addition to five junior coaches.
•5,780 young people have graduated from the programme.
•12 cycles of the course delivered.
•20 weeks of football mini-leagues and resilience sessions delivered.
•5 football pitches maintained over a seven-year period in the camp.
•100 per cent attendance rate.
Per Mertesacker
Arsenal’s Academy Manager is an ambassador for The Arsenal Foundation, and in the summer of 2019 he visited Za’atari refugee camp to launch Coaching for Life.

“Since The Arsenal Foundation began collaborating with Save the Children back in 2011, our partnership has raised more than £3.5million,” he said. “Together, we’ve helped children caught up in emergencies all over the world, bringing football to war-torn and poverty-stricken regions with the aim of providing relief from the struggles of daily life.

“My time at Za’atari refugee camp gave me an insight into where the money we raise goes. When you’re there it’s different. Circumstances are different to what you’re used to, so it can give you perspective.

“Sometimes you find it difficult to find infrastructure in refugee camps, but I saw that Save the Children was doing an excellent job in setting up an infrastructure for refugees. We as Arsenal are able to raise money and have funds to build pitches, but also have a programme in place to actually coach the coaches there, long-term. It’s also great to see that football brings joy to everyone. I forgot about the surroundings when I just played football with the children. That’s something genuine and I think it’s what we all share.

“The trip was an incredible experience for me. I’ve worked in mental hospitals throughout my life and gone into schools as a professional footballer. The more I do, the more I experience, the more I see how important it is to build up strength and partnerships with organisations that really make a difference in the world. That’s what I saw there.

“It’s just great to build something very special. It’s not just about them playing football, it’s about equipping them for life and giving them opportunities. Everyone’s been taken away from their home countries, so having a partnership with Save the Children gives them a chance. It’s such an amazing story and we should talk about it more to encourage more people to go there. We’re trying to be a role model to other clubs, other organisations, to form a strong partnership and be role models.

“Football’s not always great at supporting mental health. To build a structure is not enough. To raise money and build a pitch and then just leave them alone is not enough. We want to be there for the long-term to make a bigger impact. We need to reflect every 20 weeks to look at what they’ve done there with coaching, how we can improve their ability to coach. It’s great to see where the funds go and for me to meet youngsters and talk about how football has impacted their lives.”

items.titleZh: 生活教练
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳基金会与救助儿童会合作开展约旦扎塔里难民营项目。
bodyZh: 自2011年以来，阿森纳基金会一直与救助儿童会保持合作伙伴关系，在世界上一些条件最艰苦的地区修建球场，让那些曾遭遇暴力、迫害和艰难困苦的年轻人拥有安全的游戏和学习空间。
2019年，我们结合双方的专业知识启动了“生活教练”项目，这是我们在约旦扎塔里难民营开展的项目，该难民营收容了为逃离内战而流离失所的叙利亚人。自2011年3月以来，数百万年轻人因叙利亚残酷的内战而流离失所，许多人目睹了任何儿童都不应看到的恐怖景象。
“生活教练”项目结合了救助儿童会拥有100多年历史的儿童保护专业知识以及社区阿森纳40年的体育发展经验，通过足球来培养弱势青年的心理、情感和身体健康。
在此过程中，我们正在世界上最艰苦的环境之一开展社区项目。我们的目标过去是、现在也依然清晰：我们齐心协力让孩子们重获童年，为他们提供重建生活的工具，并指导他们走向更美好的未来。自“生活教练”项目启动以来，已有5780多名儿童从该项目毕业。
我们在伊斯灵顿的工作为我们在约旦的方法提供了指导。扎塔里难民营的教练包括来自我们教练发展项目的学员，这是一个以为期两年的阿森纳中心课程，由我们经验丰富的教练团队和行业专家提供全面的教育，并涉及在我们国内外的社区阿森纳各类项目中领导和支持训练。
阿森纳教练与救助儿童会的保护团队以及当地教练合作，探讨如何利用足球来支持儿童的身体、心理和情感健康。然而，这不仅仅是足球训练。该项目赋予儿童发声的机会，并鼓励他们捍卫自己获得安全和保护的权利。
正如阿森纳青训经理兼基金会大使默特萨克在访问约旦该项目后所说：“当儿童遭受痛苦时，我们所有人都是输家。这个项目将赋予他们勇气去应对日复一日的挣扎，并为他们提供拥有更美好未来的技能。儿童是我们的未来，我们需要与他们并肩站在一起。”
“生活教练”项目的影响是深远的。自启动以来的一些关键统计数据包括……
• 培养了48名叙利亚教练（包括36名前参与者），此外还有5名初级教练。
• 5780名年轻人从该项目毕业。
• 进行了12个周期的课程。
• 开展了为期20周的足球迷你联赛和心理韧性课程。
• 在难民营的七年时间里维护了5块足球场。
• 出勤率达到百分之百。
默特萨克
阿森纳的青训经理是阿森纳基金会的大使，在2019年夏天，他访问了扎塔里难民营以启动“生活教练”项目。
他说：“自从阿森纳基金会在2011年开始与救助儿童会合作以来，我们的伙伴关系已经筹集了超过350万英镑。我们齐心协力，帮助了世界各地陷入紧急情况的儿童，将足球带到饱受战争蹂躏和贫困困扰的地区，旨在减轻日常生活的挣扎。”
“我在扎塔里难民营的时光让我深入了解了我们筹集的资金流向何处。当你身临其境时，感觉是不同的。环境与你习惯的不同，这能带给你不同的视角。”
“有时你会发现在难民营中很难找到基础设施，但我看到救助儿童会在为难民建立基础设施方面做得非常出色。我们阿森纳能够筹集资金并拥有资金来修建球场，同时也有一个项目来真正在那里长期培训教练。同样棒的是，看到足球能给每个人带来快乐。当我只是和孩子们踢足球时，我忘记了周围的环境。那是真诚的，我认为这是我们所有人共同拥有的东西。”
“这次旅行对士我来说是一次不可思议的经历。我一生中都在精神病院工作，并作为一名职业足球运动员走进学校。我做的越多，经历的越多，我就越能看到建立力量以及与真正对世界产生影响的组织建立伙伴关系是多么重要。这就是我在那里看到的。”
“建立一些非常特别的东西真是太棒了。这不仅仅是关于他们踢足球，而是关于为他们的生活做准备并给他们机会。每个人都被迫离开他们的祖国，所以与救助儿童会建立伙伴关系给了他们一个机会。这是一个如此了不起的故事，我们应该更多地谈论它，以鼓励更多的人去那里。我们正试图成为其他俱乐部、其他组织的榜样，建立牢固的伙伴关系并成为榜样。”
“足球在支持心理健康方面并不总是做得很好。建立一个结构是不够的。筹集资金并建造一个球场然后置之不理是不够的。我们希望长期留在那里以产生更大的影响。我们需要每20周进行一次反思，看看他们在那里用教练做了什么，我们如何提高他们的执教能力。很高兴看到资金的去向，对我来说，能与年轻人见面并谈论足球如何影响他们的生活是一件很棒的事。”
